collagen  checklist  Flip the product over and check these before you buy. 01  Must say “hydrolysed” The label must say “hydrolysed collagen,” “collagen peptides,” or “collagen hydrolysate.” If it just says “collagen” it hasn’t been broken down into absorbable form. Put it back. 02 Minimum 5g per serving Check the serving size. Anything under 5g per day is below what clinical trials used to show skin benefit. Most capsule products give you 1–2g at recommended dose. That is not enough. Powder formats generally win over capsules here. 03  Type I collagen (for skin specifically) For skin you need Type I. Type I and III together is also fine. If it says Type II only that is for joints, not skin. 04  Source stated: bovine or marine Both are valid for skin. Marine (fish) collagen is Type I which is good for skin. Bovine is Type I and III which is also good. If source is not declared at all then you do not know what you are getting. 05  Vitamin C present or taken alongside Without vitamin C your body cannot properly synthesise collagen regardless of how much you supplement. Either it is in the product or take it separately every day. 06  No proprietary blend without a declared dose If it says “beauty complex” or “collagen blend” without telling you how much collagen is actually in it — the dose is being hidden because it is too small to be proud of. Walk away. Ticking all six gives you the best available option. Realistic expectation: if it is going to work for your skin, you will notice something within 8–12 weeks of consistent daily use. Nothing by then — it did not work for you. The research the checklist is based on: https://doi.org/10.3390/cosmetics11040118
